title: Exact reindexing preserves completed module resolutions and unbounded derived sheaf Hom
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_W$, $R_W=\lim_n B_{W,n}$ for a scheme $W$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $g:X\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ be a scheme isomorphism, with $\ell$ invertible on both schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Put $F=g^{-1}$, with the coefficient identifications induced by all quotient projections. Use the coefficient-stage derived operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

For $T_Y=B_{Y,n}$ with any $n\geq1$, or $T_Y=R_Y$, and corresponding $T_X$, reindexing is an exact equivalence $\operatorname{Mod}(T_Y)\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(T_X)$, preserving all small limits and colimits, flat modules, K-flat complexes and K-injective complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Its inverse is reverse reindexing. The completed coefficient identification is the ring isomorphism $FR_Y\cong R_X$ whose composite with each projection is the inverse image of $R_Y\to B_{Y,n}$ followed by the canonical finite coefficient identification. Both composites with reverse reindexing are identities on these projections and on module actions. The tensor and sheaf-Hom comparisons send local sections $s\otimes t$ to $Fs\otimes Ft$ and $f$ to $Ff$ [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom].

For an arbitrary complex $K$ and K-injective complex $I$ of $T_Y$-modules, the componentwise comparison is an isomorphism of actual Hom complexes [def-pur-hom-complex]
$$F\mathcal Hom^\bullet(K,I)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Hom^\bullet(FK,FI),\qquad F\prod_p\mathcal Hom(K^p,I^{p+r})\cong\prod_p\mathcal Hom(FK^p,FI^{p+r}).$$
It respects $d(f)=d_If-(-1)^rf d_K$ and the quasi-isomorphism invariance in both inputs. It therefore represents a natural isomorphism $c^0_{g;M,N}:FH_{T_Y}(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{T_X}(FM,FN)$ for all $M,N$ in the ordinary unbounded derived category, independent of representatives, where $H_T=R\mathcal Hom_T$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The induced derived equivalence has shift comparison identity in each degree, and termwise unit and counit. At finite coefficients it is the specified $Lg_n^*$; for $R_Y$ this assertion concerns ordinary completed-ring inverse image, prior to comparison with quotient-tower pullback.

proof.text: Use clause 1 of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]: write $\Phi_g(U\to X)=(U\to X\xrightarrow gY)$ and $\Psi=\Phi_{g^{-1}}$. Reindex a ring sheaf $T$ and a $T$-module by $F(T)(U)=T(\Phi_gU)$, $F(M)(U)=M(\Phi_gU)$, with $a\cdot m$ the original action over $\Phi_gU$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Reverse reindexing $G$ uses $\Psi$. The canonical $\Phi_g\Psi\cong1$, $\Psi\Phi_g\cong1$ give $GF\cong1$, $FG\cong1$ on rings, actions and module maps: their section maps are the original restriction identifications and hence are linear. This proves the module equivalence for every ring sheaf $T$, including a nonconstant completed one; it does not extend only the constant-module clause of the cited lemma without an argument.

source.place: Step 1, exact automorphism pullback; explicit lifting to arbitrary ring-sheaf modules

proof.text: For any small diagram $D$ of modules, a cone from $P$ to $FD$ corresponds, by the equivalence of step 1, to a cone from $GP$ to $D$. Thus $F(\lim D)$ has the limit universal property. Applying the same Hom bijections to cocones proves preservation of colimits. Reindexing is additive since sectionwise addition is unchanged. Kernels and cokernels are the limits and colimits of the relevant two-arrow diagrams, so $F$ and $G$ are exact. In particular $H^r(FK)\cong F(H^rK)$ from the kernel/image/quotient definition in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; both functors preserve acyclic complexes and quasi-isomorphisms. No exactness of infinite products is being asserted. In Lean the specified forward/inverse equivalence is supplied by podReindexing_roundTrip_shift. Its IsEquivalence instance gives preservation of limits and colimits in every requested universe; finite exactness is already supplied by isoSectionwiseModuleInverseImage_exact.

source.place: Step 1, consequences of the explicit reindexing equivalence

proof.text: By clause 3 of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], $c_n:FB_{Y,n}\cong B_{X,n}$ is compatible with every quotient map. By [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], $R_W$ is the ring-sheaf limit of this tower. Consequently step 2 gives the unique ring isomorphism $c_R:FR_Y\cong R_X$ with $\pi_{X,n}c_R=c_nF(\pi_{Y,n})$. Apply the same construction to $g^{-1}$. Each composite with reverse reindexing has projection $\pi_{W,n}$, since both the constant coefficient identifications and their reductions are the canonical ones. Uniqueness of maps into the limit makes the composites identities, under the reindexing unit identifications. Transport a module action via $c_R^{-1}$; after the two transports its scalar map is the identity, so its action is the original action. The identical assertion at $B_{W,n}$ follows using $c_n$. In the Lean round-trip proof, equality at a finite stage is checked on the constant-presheaf sheafification unit, after cancelling the canonical reindexing/sheafification isomorphism. Naturality of that unit gives the site return restriction. The completed case then follows by projecting to every finite stage and applying limit.hom_ext.

Apply [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom] with the ring sheaf $T_Y$ and then the coefficient isomorphism of step 3. This supplies the tensor and sheaf-Hom isomorphisms for $T_Y=B_{Y,n}$ or $R_Y$. They send the inverse images of $s\otimes t$ and $f$ to $Fs\otimes Ft$ and $Ff$, respectively, and are natural in both module inputs. If $P$ is flat, tensoring any exact sequence $A$ on $X$ with $FP$ identifies with $F(GA\otimes P)$: $GA$ is exact by step 2 and $-\otimes P$ is exact by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Thus $FP$ is flat. Interchanging $F$ and $G$ proves the converse. The flatness preservation clause, together with Step 5, is isolated in [lem-pod-sectionwise-flat-kflat] for arbitrary commutative ring sheaves and invertible coefficient identifications.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; Tag 0GMX, remark-pullback-internal-hom; specialize existing site-isomorphism comparison

proof.text: For complexes $A,P$, the total tensor in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] is the direct sum of $A^p\otimes P^q$ over $p+q=r$, with differential $d_A\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_P$. Steps 2 and 4 therefore identify $F\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes P)$ with $\operatorname{Tot}(FA\otimes FP)$; both differential summands agree by tensor naturality and additivity. If $P$ is K-flat and $C$ is any acyclic complex on $X$, put $A=GC$. It is acyclic, hence $A\otimes P$ is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex], and the displayed identification gives $C\otimes FP\cong F(A\otimes P)$ acyclic. Thus $FP$ is K-flat. Reverse the roles to get reflection. A K-flat resolution remains one because its augmentation remains a quasi-isomorphism by step 2. Apply [lem-pod-sectionwise-flat-kflat] to podReindexingCoefficient to obtain this clause at either coefficient stage.

source.place: Step 1, K-flat preservation for unbounded direct-sum tensor complexes

proof.text: Let $I$ be K-injective and let $a:C\to FI$ be a map from an arbitrary acyclic complex on $X$. Under step 1 it corresponds to $b:GC\to I$. Since $GC$ is acyclic, [def-pur-kinjective-complex] gives $h^p:(GC)^p\to I^{p-1}$ with $b^p=d_I^{p-1}h^p+h^{p+1}d_{GC}^p$. Applying $F$ and conjugating by the degreewise equivalence identifications gives $a^p=d_{FI}^{p-1}(Fh)^p+(Fh)^{p+1}d_C^p$. Hence $FI$ is K-injective. The same calculation for $G$ proves reflection. Since quasi-isomorphisms are preserved, $N\to I$ is carried to a K-injective resolution $FN\to FI$. The Lean proof uses the adjunction from the reverse module equivalence: transpose a map from an acyclic complex, use the defining null homotopy, and transport it through the forward functor and adjunction unit. This is the direct proof of the K-injective clause; no new K-injective theorem is assumed. The Lean proof uses the already proved source-library theorem CochainComplex.isKInjective_map_of_adjunction with left adjoint e.inverse; its proof is exactly this transposition and null-homotopy argument.

source.place: Step 1, K-injective preservation by transporting the defining null homotopy

proof.text: For each integer $r$, preserve the product over all $p\in\mathbf Z$ by step 2 and apply the sheaf-Hom comparison of step 4 to each factor. This gives $c^r:F\prod_p\mathcal Hom_{T_Y}(K^p,I^{p+r})\cong\prod_p\mathcal Hom_{T_X}(FK^p,FI^{p+r})$, the terms of the Hom complexes defined in [def-pur-hom-complex]. Its $p$-th projection is the inverse image of the $p$-th Hom projection followed by the normalized comparison, so it sends a family $(f^p)_p$ to $(Ff^p)_p$. The product is countable in the fixed universe; neither input complex is assumed bounded.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes; actual product complex, with Tag 0GMX normalization

proof.text: For a homogeneous family $f$ of degree $r$, naturality of the sheaf-Hom comparisons and additivity give, in the $p$-th factor, $F(d_I^{p+r}f^p-(-1)^rf^{p+1}d_K^p)=d_{FI}^{p+r}Ff^p-(-1)^rFf^{p+1}d_{FK}^p$. Product projections jointly determine maps. Thus $c^{r+1}F(d)=d c^r$, and the component isomorphisms of step 7 are an isomorphism of actual complexes, not merely isomorphisms of cohomology sheaves. For maps $a:K'\to K$ and $b:I\to I'$, the same projection calculation is $F(bfa)=Fb\,Ff\,Fa$, proving joint naturality.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes: the differential and its functoriality

proof.text: If $t:K'\to K$ and $s:I\to I'$ are quasi-isomorphisms with $I,I'$ K-injective, [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] makes $f\mapsto sft$ a quasi-isomorphism of sheaf Hom complexes. Its inverse image remains a quasi-isomorphism by step 2; the Hom map after reindexing is one by the same cited lemma and step 6. Step 8 identifies these maps, which proves the asserted compatibility with quasi-isomorphism invariance in both inputs. Here the second-variable comparison is between K-injective resolutions; no claim is used that $\mathcal Hom(K,-)$ preserves arbitrary quasi-isomorphisms.

Choose $K$ representing $M$ and a resolution $N\to I$ supplied by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. By step 6, $FN\to FI$ is an allowed resolution for $FN$. Therefore [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] identifies the two complexes of step 8 with $FH_{T_Y}(M,N)$ and $H_{T_X}(FM,FN)$. Localize the isomorphism to obtain $c^0_{g;M,N}$. Step 9 and the canonical independence of representatives and K-injective resolutions in the cited definition identify the result for every other choice. Naturality holds for complex maps by step 8 and for inverses of quasi-isomorphisms by step 9, hence for every derived morphism by the localization universal property [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This proves the required natural derived isomorphism for arbitrary unbounded inputs.

source.place: Tags 079I (injectives-section-K-injective), 08J7 (section-internal-hom), 0A95 (lemma-RHom-well-defined); assembly in the localized category

proof.text: Apply $F,G$ termwise to complexes. Their unit and counit of step 1 are chain maps because they are natural for every differential; their triangle identities hold in each degree. They pass to the localization since step 2 preserves quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Also $(FK[1])^p=F(K^{p+1})=(F(K[1]))^p$, and both differentials are $-F(d_K)$, so the shift comparison is the identity in each degree, and likewise for every integer shift. At finite coefficients, [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] specifies exactly the termwise inverse image with action along $c_n$, which is the functor just constructed. At $R_Y$, the construction was on all ordinary $R_Y$-module complexes; no identification with the quotient-tower completed pullback has been used. In Lean the inverse coefficient maps feed SheafOfModules.pushforwardPushforwardEquivalence, with the scalar triangle identities deduced from the ring round trips. Its unit and counit evaluate to the stated restrictions. Equivalence.mapDerivedCategory supplies the termwise derived equivalence. For the finite comparison use the section-normalized finiteSectionwiseAdjunction from [lem-weil-finite-comparison-complex-isomorphism]: uniqueness of left adjoints compares the normalized sectionwise module functor with sfIntrinsicPullback, and Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso localizes that comparison.
